cards.title: Fitness Training
cards.intro: Strong legs, a strong heart and a strong mind. Start training at least 12–16 weeks before departure.
items: Aerobic base: 3–4 sessions weekly of hiking, running or cycling
Weighted-pack hikes with 10–15 kg on hilly terrain, building to 6+ hours
Leg strength: lunges, step-ups and squats twice per week
Core and balance work to protect your back under load
Practise back-to-back long days to simulate expedition fatigue

cards.title: Gear List
cards.intro: Quality over quantity. Every item should earn its place in your pack.
items: Layering system: base, insulating mid, hardshell and a down jacket
Mountaineering boots that are correctly fitted and well broken in
Helmet, harness, crampons, ice axe and carabiners (we supply on request)
Sleeping bag rated 5 °C colder than the expected minimum
Headtorch, sunglasses (category 4), sunscreen, and spare batteries

cards.title: Permits & Documents
cards.intro: Regulations vary widely. We handle permits, but you must bring valid documents.
items: Passport valid for at least six months beyond your return date
Peak and national-park permits arranged by Alpine Ascents
Visas and vaccination records where required
Digital and paper copies of all documents, stored separately
Emergency contacts and medical information card

cards.title: Leave No Trace
cards.intro: The mountains are not ours to keep. Leave them better than you found them.
items: Pack out everything you pack in, including human waste where required
Stay on established trails and camp on durable surfaces
Use stoves rather than fires; respect all wildlife
Respect local cultures, shrines and communities
Leave what you find, from rocks to prayer flags

cards.title: Insurance
cards.intro: Rescue and evacuation can cost tens of thousands. Insurance is mandatory on every expedition.
items: Policy must cover mountaineering up to your maximum altitude
Helicopter evacuation and repatriation cover must be included
Trip cancellation and interruption cover is strongly recommended
Carry your policy number and the insurer's 24-hour emergency line
Check exclusions carefully: some require a guide or specific certification

cards.title: Emergency Protocol
cards.intro: Know what to do before something goes wrong. Your guide leads, but everyone must be prepared.
items: Stop, assess, and make the scene safe before helping anyone
Alert your guide immediately; never leave a sick team-member alone
Use the satellite messenger or radio to call for help, giving location and condition
Descend early for altitude sickness. Descent saves lives
Follow the guide's evacuation plan and keep the group together
